### MTX-082 - AC-PRULE-031 (PRULE: PRULE-031)

- Slice: S-16,S-20
- Status: Complete
- contract owner: specification/volume-ii/SECURITY_PERFORMANCE.md#prule-031-cross-surface-visibility-and-redaction-parity
- interface type: Cross-surface parity rule. PRULE-031 governs CAP-018 and CAP-022 and applies to WF-010, WF-012 and WF-016. It adds no command and defines no new visibility semantics -- it requires the semantics MTX-050 owns to produce IDENTICAL outcomes on EVERY delivery surface. It has NO decision dependency, so nothing is withheld.
- route: Not applicable - PRULE-031 is a rule, not an interface. It binds every surface whatever routes API_CONTRACTS.md defines.
- request schema: Not applicable - constrains the response of every delivery surface, not one request shape.
- response schema: Not applicable - requires the MTX-050 outcome set to be identical across surfaces: the same object denial, the same omitted fields, the same stable codes, the same reference-only Evidence and the same allowed values.
- controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter is authorized by Volume I.
- command: Not applicable - PRULE-031 constrains reads and deliveries and adds no command.
- command input: Not applicable - no command.
- command output: Not applicable - no command.
- actor: Every reading actor on every surface. PRULE-031's Owner is the Chief Security; that is governance ownership of the rule, not a runtime actor.
- organization scope: The reading or receiving principal's Organization. Parity includes tenant scoping: a surface that is correct on fields but loose on Organization scope has not achieved parity.
- aggregate: Not applicable as a write root - the rule owns no aggregate. It constrains reads and deliveries of score, Issue, Recommendation, history and Evidence data.
- aggregate boundary: The rule's boundary is the SET OF SURFACES, not a record. Volume I names them exactly: UI read models, logical API responses, EXPORTS, NOTIFICATIONS and SUPPORT VIEWS. Exports and notifications are the two that drift, because each has an independent serialization path and a delivery mechanism that outlives the request that authorized it -- a notification is composed once and delivered later, and an Export is generated once and retrieved later.
- value objects: DataClassification, ClassificationCeiling, RedactedFieldCode, AccessStatus, DeliverySurface, ExportManifestField, NotificationPayloadField, SupportSessionScope.
- domain service: Not applicable - PRULE-031 names no domain service. Its whole content is that ONE function is applied everywhere rather than reimplemented per surface, so a second per-surface implementation is the defect it exists to prevent.
- repository: Read-only access to the same repositories MTX-050 names, from every surface. No surface reads a private denormalized copy.
- persistence model: Not applicable as a new concept - the rule introduces no record. It is why an Export persists only its separate WF-016 logical manifest and lifecycle records rather than a pre-redacted snapshot of customer data: a stored pre-redacted copy would freeze one actor's ceiling into a durable artifact that a differently-privileged actor might later retrieve.
- migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added by this row. A per-surface redaction configuration table MUST NOT be migrated: configurable per-surface rules are exactly how surfaces drift, and PRULE-031 requires identical outcomes rather than separately-configured ones.
- transaction boundary: Each surface applies the redaction decision inside its own read or generation transaction, before serialization. A notification's payload is redacted at composition against the RECIPIENT's role, and an Export's content is redacted at generation against the REQUESTER's role -- neither inherits the redaction of the surface that triggered it.
- concurrency: Each surface resolves the actor's role once, at its own authorization entry point. A role change between an Export request and its retrieval does not retroactively re-redact stored content; the Export's retrieval authorization is checked independently under `export.retrieve`, which is why an Export must not store data above what its retriever may see.
- idempotency: The rule has no key of its own: because redaction is a pure function of role and classification, the same actor and the same records yield the same outcome on every surface and on every repetition. Parity is a consequence of that purity, and a surface that caches or reimplements the function breaks it.
- background job: Notification composition and Export generation run asynchronously and are exactly where parity is tested, because each redacts outside the original request. Raw Evidence payloads, secrets, verification tokens, provider credentials and unrestricted internal errors are PROHIBITED from a Notification payload.
- queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own; the notification and export queues are owned by BACKGROUND_PROCESSING.md and are not renamed here.
- retry policy: Not applicable - a redaction outcome is not retried. A notification retry re-delivers the SAME already-redacted payload and MUST NOT recompose it against a different role.
- terminal failure: INCONSISTENT SURFACE REDACTION is a CAP-018 Failure Condition in its own right -- a surface returning MORE than another for the same actor and records is a failure even if every individual field it returned was independently permitted. That is the precise defect this rule names, and it is why parity is asserted by comparing surfaces rather than by checking each surface alone.
- reconciliation: The same allow, omit and deny semantics apply to UI read models, logical API responses, exports, notifications and support views. `Every visibility fixture in AC-SM-007 produces identical authorization and redaction outcomes across all surfaces` -- AC-PRULE-031 defines itself entirely by reference to AC-SM-007's fixture set, so the rule adds no new fixture content and instead multiplies the existing set by the surface count.
- domain events: Not applicable - PRULE-031 emits no event of its own. It constrains the payload of notifications the notification pipeline delivers and the content of Exports WF-016 produces.
- event payload: Not applicable - no event of its own. It does constrain the Notification payload: raw Evidence payloads, secrets, verification tokens, provider credentials and unrestricted internal errors are prohibited from it.
- event producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- event consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- serializer: Every serializer on every surface -- UI read model, logical API, export, notification and support view -- applies the SAME redaction decision, handed to it, never re-derived inside it. A serializer that re-derives is the mechanism of drift.
- authorization entry point: Each surface's own read or generation path, before serialization, resolving that surface's actor -- the reader for a UI or API read, the RECIPIENT for a notification, the REQUESTER for an Export, the session-scoped operator for a support view. The rule is that each entry point applies the same function, not that they share one entry point.
- permission checks: The same Permission Baseline cells and the same classification ceilings apply on every surface; no surface has its own permission set. `export.create`, `export.retrieve` and `export.list` govern reaching the export surface, and the Executive Buyer is SUMMARY-ONLY on export while being allow-through-`internal` on reads -- a surface-specific PERMISSION difference that is not a redaction difference, and the two must not be conflated. A SecurityOperator's export access is `security-authorized only`. BillingOperator is deny on export as on everything else.
- tenant boundary: Organization scope is mandatory on every surface. An Export or notification delivered outside the Organization is a cross-tenant disclosure regardless of its field-level correctness.
- error contract: An object denial returns `F1-AUTH-403` with one authorization audit event on every surface. Field omission carries the same stable codes on every surface. Reference-only Evidence returns `evidence_id` and `access_status=restricted` on every surface. The outcome vocabulary does not vary by surface.
- audit record: Each surface emits its own access and redaction telemetry, and each denial emits exactly one authorization audit event on the surface where it occurred. The audit records the surface, so a parity breach is attributable to a specific surface rather than merely detected.
- observability: Because the stable code groups are identical across surfaces, a parity breach is observable by DIFFING the code lists two surfaces return for the same actor and records -- which is how the cross-surface fixtures assert it, rather than by inspecting each surface in isolation.
- retention: Not applicable - PRULE-031 defines no retention. Export lifecycle records and notification records are retained under their own contracts; the windows are owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md.
- test contracts: TYP-E2E: EVERY visibility fixture in AC-SM-007 produces IDENTICAL authorization and redaction outcomes across ALL FIVE surfaces -- UI read models, logical API responses, exports, notifications and support views; the AC-SM-007 fixture set is multiplied by five and each result is asserted byte-identical in its allowed field set and its `redacted_field_codes` list. TYP-SEC: INCONSISTENT SURFACE REDACTION is asserted to be a failure IN ITS OWN RIGHT -- a fixture where one surface returns MORE than another for the same actor and records fails, even though every field it returned was independently permitted; asserted by DIFFING surfaces rather than by checking each alone, because per-surface checks pass while parity fails. TYP-SEC: a notification payload is redacted at COMPOSITION against the RECIPIENT's role, not against the role of whoever triggered it -- asserted with a trigger by a high-ceiling actor and a delivery to a low-ceiling recipient. TYP-SEC: an Export's content is redacted at GENERATION against the REQUESTER's role. TYP-SEC: a notification RETRY re-delivers the SAME already-redacted payload and is asserted NOT to recompose against a different role. TYP-SEC: an Export must not store data above what its retriever may see -- asserted because retrieval is authorized independently under `export.retrieve` and a role change between request and retrieval must not disclose more. TYP-SEC: raw Evidence payloads, secrets, verification tokens, provider credentials and unrestricted internal errors are asserted ABSENT from every Notification payload -- five assertions. TYP-DATA: no surface reads a private denormalized copy; all surfaces read the same canonical projections. TYP-DATA: a per-surface redaction configuration table is asserted ABSENT -- configurable per-surface rules are the mechanism of drift and the rule requires identical outcomes rather than separately-configured ones. TYP-DATA: every serializer is handed the redaction decision and is asserted NOT to re-derive it. TYP-SEC: the outcome vocabulary does not vary by surface -- `F1-AUTH-403` with one audit event for an object denial, the same stable codes for omission, and `evidence_id` plus `access_status=restricted` for reference-only, all asserted identical on all five surfaces. TYP-SEC: a surface-specific PERMISSION difference is not a redaction difference -- the Executive Buyer is SUMMARY-ONLY on export while allow-through-`internal` on reads, and SecurityOperator export access is `security-authorized only`; asserted that these are permission cells and that the redaction FUNCTION applied within them is still identical, because conflating the two is how a surface justifies its own rules. TYP-SEC: BillingOperator is deny on export as on every other surface. TYP-SEC: Organization scope is mandatory on every surface; an Export or notification delivered outside the Organization is a cross-tenant disclosure regardless of field-level correctness. TYP-OBS: each denial emits exactly one authorization audit event RECORDING ITS SURFACE, so a parity breach is attributable rather than merely detected. TYP-E2E: the code lists two surfaces return for the same actor and records are asserted equal by direct diff.
- rollout: PRULE-031 governs CAP-018 and CAP-022 and applies to WF-010, WF-012 and WF-016. S-16 owns this row: the parity obligation across all five delivery surfaces. The Export and Sharing slice consumes it for the WF-016 surface and the Historical Comparison slice for the WF-012 surface; neither is contracted here. The visibility semantics themselves are MTX-050's. Nothing is withheld: the matrix records no decision dependency for PRULE-031.

### MTX-083 - AC-PRULE-032 (PRULE: PRULE-032)

- Slice: S-17
- Status: Complete
- contract owner: specification/volume-ii/SECURITY_PERFORMANCE.md#prule-032-comparison-compatibility-and-rebase
- interface type: A cross-surface invariant over the comparison read, not an interface. PRULE-032 binds every reader of historical data regardless of surface or permission: comparison uses state-at-snapshot data only, returns no numeric delta unless EVERY required dimension matches, returns all fixed-order mismatch codes when they do not, and rebase requires all target versions and can never overcome different normalized scope hashes. It is enforced at the point the compatibility predicate is evaluated on MTX-037, and it is owned here because its failure mode - a silently comparable cross-version pair - is a correctness and integrity breach rather than a workflow step.
- route: Not applicable - a rule constrains every surface that returns a comparison and mints no route of its own. The physical route is owned by API_CONTRACTS.md; see MTX-037's route.
- request schema: Not applicable - the rule constrains the response and the predicate, not the request shape. The one request-side clause it owns is the rebase's: an exact target version for every one of the seven versioned dimensions, each available to both retained input sets, with omission or ambiguity rejecting the request. The `QRY-008` query shape is contracted on MTX-037.
- response schema: The rule fixes exactly two response-side facts. First, `mismatch_codes` contains EVERY applicable code from the closed set of eight, in this exact fixed order: `score_policy_mismatch`, `confidence_policy_mismatch`, `eligibility_policy_mismatch`, `fingerprint_version_mismatch`, `check_catalog_version_mismatch`, `scope_policy_version_set_mismatch`, `scope_definition_mismatch`, `pillar_applicability_mismatch`. Second, a `not_comparable` result contains NO numeric score delta - `overall_delta` is null and `pillar_deltas` is empty. The `HistoryItemDTO` carries the eight comparable dimensions as `score_policy_version`, `confidence_policy_version`, `eligibility_policy_version`, `fingerprint_version`, `check_catalog_version`, `scope_policy_version_set_hash`, `scope_definition_hash` and `pillar_applicability_version`, which is what makes the predicate independently checkable from the response itself.
- controller: Not applicable - the rule is enforced in the comparison predicate, not in an HTTP adapter; no controller is defined by Volume I. See MTX-037.
- command: The rule contributes no command. It constrains the rebase command's admission - all seven target versions exact and available to both retained input sets - and constrains its reach: rebase can never make different normalized `scope_definition_hash` values comparable. The snapshots an admitted rebase creates are MTX-076's in S-13.
- command input: Not applicable - the rule adds no command envelope field. The rebase envelope is contracted on MTX-037.
- command output: Not applicable - the rule adds no command result field. The rebase result is contracted on MTX-037.
- actor: The rule binds every actor with no exception: OrganizationAdmin, MarketingOperator, TechnicalImplementer, read-only Executive Buyer, authorized SecurityOperator scope and any tenant-scoped service identity are each subject to the identical compatibility predicate. No role sees a delta another role may not, because compatibility is a property of the two snapshots and not of the reader. `score.rebase` authorizes an OrganizationAdmin to CREATE compatible snapshots; it does not authorize reading a delta across incompatible ones.
- organization scope: Both snapshots resolve to one Organization and one Project before the predicate is evaluated; a cross-Organization pair is a tenant failure and never a mismatch code. See MTX-037's organization_scope.
- aggregate: No aggregate - the rule is an invariant over two immutable ScoreSnapshot roots owned by MTX-076 in S-13. No Comparison aggregate exists in the domain model, state model or schema.
- aggregate boundary: The rule's boundary is what a rebase may reach. A rebase may create new immutable noncurrent snapshots under exact requested versions for the seven versioned dimensions; it may NOT mutate an original snapshot, advance a current pointer, or align a normalized `scope_definition_hash`. That last exclusion is the load-bearing one: seven dimensions are versioned policy that a rebase can re-run the calculation under, but the scope-definition hash is a normalized description of WHAT was measured, and two evaluations of different scopes are not the same measurement under a different policy. A rebase that could align it would silently redefine the subject rather than the method.
- value objects: MismatchCode restricted to the eight fixed-order codes; ScorePolicyVersion, ConfidencePolicyVersion, EligibilityPolicyVersion, FingerprintVersion, CheckCatalogVersion, ScopePolicyVersionSetSha256, ScopeDefinitionSha256 and PillarApplicabilityVersion as the eight compared dimensions; RebaseTargetVersionSet as the seven exact requestable versions. Note the asymmetry the rule fixes: eight dimensions are compared, seven are rebaseable, and `scope_definition_hash` is the one that is compared and never rebaseable.
- domain service: Not applicable - the rule names no domain service. Compatibility is a pure equality predicate over eight frozen values and the mismatch list is a pure ordered projection of its failures; neither is a collaborator with a lifecycle.
- repository: As MTX-037's repositories, read-only. The rule adds none. The eight compared dimensions are frozen columns on `score_snapshots`, so the predicate needs no additional read.
- persistence model: The eight compared dimensions are frozen on the immutable `score_snapshots` row (`T-IMM`, `LINEAGE`) per schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md, which carries the Evaluation, Issue Set, Catalog, applicability and policy IDs and hashes. Their immutability is what makes the predicate reproducible: a comparison run today and in seven years over the same pair returns the same status and codes. The rule persists nothing itself.
- migration: Not applicable at this row - the rule adds no schema object; the eight dimensions already exist as frozen columns. See MTX-037's migration.
- transaction boundary: The predicate is evaluated inside MTX-037's single authorized read transaction, over rows already materialized; it opens no transaction of its own and performs no write. An admitted rebase's snapshot creation is S-13's transaction.
- concurrency: The predicate reads only immutable frozen columns, so it has no race: no concurrent write can change whether two given snapshots are compatible, which is why the answer is stable forever rather than merely at read time. A concurrently created rebase snapshot is a NEW pair to compare, never a mutation of an existing comparison.
- idempotency: The predicate is a pure function of the two snapshots' eight frozen dimensions and therefore returns the identical status and identical ordered code list on every evaluation, with no key required. Rebase idempotency belongs to the ScoreSnapshot idempotency tuple on MTX-076: exact replay returns the existing pair, and reuse under a different canonical request hash is `idempotency_conflict`.
- background job: Not applicable - the rule defines no background job and no asynchronous work; the predicate is evaluated synchronously in the read.
- queue: Not applicable - no background job is defined at this row, so no queue class is claimed. See background_job.
- retry policy: Not applicable - the predicate is deterministic and total over its inputs, so it has no transient failure to retry: `not_comparable` is a correct terminal answer and retrying it returns the same answer. A rejected rebase is not retried implicitly under inferred versions; a new rebase is a new explicit command with its own exact target versions.
- terminal failure: A pair failing any one of the eight equalities is `not_comparable` with every applicable code and no numeric delta - terminal for that pair unless a rebase creates a new one, and permanently terminal when `scope_definition_mismatch` is among the codes. A rebase omitting or ambiguating any of the seven target versions, or naming one unavailable to either retained input set, is rejected and creates no snapshot. A state failing the predicate but matching no defined code cannot occur, because the eight codes exhaustively cover the eight compared dimensions; the comparison mints no ninth code and infers no delta from a partial match.
- reconciliation: The rule is total in both directions and that totality is the point. A `comparable` result means all eight equalities held, so a delta is attributable to real change rather than to a policy shift. A `not_comparable` result names EVERY dimension that diverged, not the first found, so a caller can tell in one response whether a rebase would help - seven codes are rebaseable, `scope_definition_mismatch` never is - rather than discovering a permanent barrier only after an authorized rebase completes. There is no third state in which a pair is compared under partial agreement.
- domain events: Exactly zero - the rule emits no event and, under OD-024, neither does the comparison it constrains. A mismatch is reported in the response and the audit record, never as a domain event. See MTX-037's domain_events.
- event payload: Not applicable - this row emits no domain event. See domain_events.
- event producer: Not applicable - this row emits no domain event and no producer exists. See domain_events.
- event consumers: Not applicable - no event is produced, so no consumer subscribes. See domain_events.
- serializer: The `mismatch_codes` array in `HistoryComparisonDTO`, typed as a closed enum of exactly the eight codes with a `[0..8]` bound, serialized in the fixed order rather than in discovery order or sorted alphabetically. The eight compared dimensions are themselves serialized on each `HistoryItemDTO`, so a caller can independently verify the predicate against the response. Serialization emits no delta field value for `not_comparable`.
- authorization entry point: The comparison predicate itself, evaluated on every comparison before any delta is computed and independently of the actor's permission - the rule is an invariant, not an authorization check, so no grant relaxes it. Rebase authorization is a separate check at the rebase command: `score.rebase`, verified there and never inherited from the read that produced the `not_comparable` result.
- permission checks: `score.rebase`, held by an OrganizationAdmin only. The Permission Baseline denies it to MarketingOperator, TechnicalImplementer, SecurityOperator, BillingOperator and the Read-Only Executive Buyer, and admits only 'scoring service executes authorized request only' - the service executes an authorized request and originates none. `history.read` never substitutes for `score.rebase`. Critically, NO permission - including `score.rebase` - authorizes a numeric delta across a mismatched pair or across different normalized scope hashes: the rule binds every actor, and an OrganizationAdmin holding every grant in the baseline still receives `not_comparable`.
- tenant boundary: Both snapshots resolve to one Organization and one Project before the predicate runs; forced RLS on `score_snapshots` makes a cross-Organization pair unresolvable rather than incomparable. A cross-tenant reference is `F1-AUTH-403 / tenant_mismatch`, never a mismatch code - the eight codes describe version divergence within a tenant and must never be used to report a tenant failure, which would leak the existence of another Organization's snapshot.
- error contract: The rule's outcomes are STATUSES, not error envelopes: `not_comparable` with its ordered codes is a successful deterministic response and returning `F1-VALIDATION-400` or `F1-DOMAIN-409` for an incompatible pair would destroy the mismatch-code contract that tells a caller what to fix. The rule's own error surface is the rebase's: `F1-VALIDATION-400` for an omitted or ambiguous target version or one unavailable to either retained input set, changing no state and creating no snapshot; `F1-AUTH-403` for a rebase without `score.rebase`. A cross-Organization snapshot reference is `F1-AUTH-403 / tenant_mismatch`. If the predicate could somehow select no code for a failed equality the workflow returns `F1-DATA-409 / contract_invariant_unmapped` and commits no side effect rather than returning a delta under partial agreement; no invented reason code is exposed outward.
- audit record: Per WF-012's Audit and Observability, the compatibility INPUTS and the result are audited alongside the mismatch codes and the rebase snapshot IDs - the inputs, not only the verdict, which is what makes a disputed `not_comparable` result reconstructible without re-reading the snapshots. Every rejected rebase is audited with its exact reason, including which target version was omitted, ambiguous or unavailable. Comparison audit records are `product_history`.
- observability: The eight fixed-order codes are the observable signal: a `not_comparable` outcome names precisely which dimensions diverged and therefore whether a rebase is possible, and the order is itself part of the contract so that two implementations produce identical, diffable output. Rebase snapshot IDs and retry count are observable in the audit record. No domain event carries any of this, per OD-024. The predicate adds no SQL to the registered `QRY-008` budget of 9 statements and 500 rows because it reads columns already materialized for the response.
- retention: The eight compared dimensions are frozen columns on `score_snapshots`, a `product_history` record retained 7 years on a cursor of 7 elapsed years after record creation or terminal transition, whichever is later, per 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md. Rebase snapshots enter the same class. The rule persists nothing of its own and states no new window; 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md owns it.
- test contracts: TYP-DATA: the compatibility predicate is exact and total - a pair is `comparable` ONLY when all eight of score policy, confidence policy, eligibility policy, fingerprint, check-catalog, scope-policy version set, normalized `scope_definition_hash` and pillar-applicability versions are identical; asserted with a fixture that matches on seven and diverges on one, once per dimension, each returning `not_comparable`. TYP-DATA: the code ORDER is fixed and asserted as a sequence, not a set - `score_policy_mismatch`, `confidence_policy_mismatch`, `eligibility_policy_mismatch`, `fingerprint_version_mismatch`, `check_catalog_version_mismatch`, `scope_policy_version_set_mismatch`, `scope_definition_mismatch`, `pillar_applicability_mismatch`; asserted for every combination including all eight diverging at once and for pairs whose divergent dimensions are discovered in a different physical column order. TYP-DATA: `not_comparable` returns NO numeric score delta - `overall_delta` null and `pillar_deltas` empty; asserted for every mismatch combination, so no partial-agreement delta ever leaks. TYP-DATA: state-at-snapshot only - the predicate reads the two snapshots' frozen dimensions and a later Issue, adjudication or Evidence decision changes neither the status nor the codes; asserted by comparing before and after such a decision. TYP-DATA: an authorized rebase supplying all seven exact target versions available to both retained input sets creates two immutable noncurrent snapshots and the resulting pair compares `comparable`. TYP-DATA: rebase rejection - omission of any one of the seven target versions, ambiguity on any one, and a version unavailable to either retained input set each reject the request and create NO snapshot; asserted once per dimension for each of the three rejection modes. TYP-DATA: rebase can NEVER overcome different normalized `scope_definition_hash` values - a fully specified, fully authorized, all-version rebase over a pair differing only in scope-definition hash still returns `not_comparable` with `scope_definition_mismatch`; asserted as permanent, with no next action that would resolve it. TYP-DATA: `scope_definition_mismatch` present in the codes means `request_rebase` is not returned as a next action, so the response never suggests an action that cannot succeed. TYP-DATA: a rebase never mutates an original snapshot and never advances a Current Score Projection pointer; both originals are asserted byte-identical after the rebase and the projection's pointers unchanged. TYP-INT: the predicate is pure and reproducible - the same pair evaluated twice returns identical status and identical ordered codes, and evaluation performs no write. TYP-INT: the eight compared dimensions are present on each `HistoryItemDTO` so the predicate is independently verifiable from the response alone. TYP-INT: `mismatch_codes` is a closed enum bounded `[0..8]` with no duplicate and no ninth code; an unmapped divergence is asserted impossible rather than serialized as a new code. TYP-INT: `mismatch_codes` is empty exactly when status is `comparable`. TYP-SEC: the rule binds every actor - an OrganizationAdmin holding `score.rebase` and every other baseline grant still receives `not_comparable` and no delta for a mismatched pair; no permission relaxes the predicate. TYP-SEC: `score.rebase` is denied to MarketingOperator, TechnicalImplementer, SecurityOperator, BillingOperator and the Read-Only Executive Buyer; `history.read` is not accepted as rebase authority. TYP-SEC: a cross-Organization or cross-Project snapshot pair returns `F1-AUTH-403 / tenant_mismatch` and is asserted NEVER to return a mismatch code, so no code discloses the existence of another tenant's snapshot.
- rollout: S-17 depends on S-16 and gates nothing. This row owns the compatibility predicate, the eight fixed-order mismatch codes and the rebase admission and reach rules for the whole slice; MTX-037 evaluates the predicate inside the WF-012 read and MTX-019 cites it as the guard against CAP-019's silent-cross-version-comparison Failure Condition. The snapshots an admitted rebase creates are MTX-076's (AC-PRULE-025, S-13 Scoring), consumed here and not redefined. PRULE-032's decision dependencies are OD-002, OD-003 and OD-009, each ratified, plus OD-024; it withholds nothing. No predecessor behaviour exists.

### MTX-085 - AC-PRULE-034 (PRULE: PRULE-034)

- Slice: S-01,S-19,S-23
- Status: Complete; limb withheld
- Withheld limb: UPSTREAM-V1-CREDENTIAL-ROTATION-TOKEN-009 (OD-023) -- OD-023: credential rotation begin/complete withheld; other Credential lifecycle permitted
- contract owner: specification/volume-ii/SECURITY_PERFORMANCE.md#prule-034-notification-delivery-authority

This row owns its CAP-021/WF-014 limb; the WF-013 Invitation and Role limb is owned by S-01 and S-23 and invokes this contract's delivery path rather than reimplementing it. Its owner is Chief Security. It has no decision dependency of its own beyond those the register cites.
- route: Not applicable - PRULE-034 is a rule, not an interface.
- request schema: Not applicable - the rule constrains the MTX-039 schema rather than defining one.
- response schema: Not applicable - see request_schema.
- controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter.
- command: Enforced within `ConsumeNotificationEvent`, `ExecuteDeliveryAttempt`, `ReconcileDelivery`, `ConsumeProviderEvent` and `RequestNotificationReplay`. This row adds no command.
- command input: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-039 input.
- command output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-039 output.
- actor: As MTX-039 per command. The rule is actor-scoped in one specific respect it states itself: administrative replay of an uncertain Delivery requires explicit duplicate-risk acknowledgment from the replaying SecurityOperator, so the acknowledgment is an actor obligation rather than a system default.
- organization scope: The event Organization; selectors resolve Accounts within that Organization and resource scope only.
- aggregate: Notification and Delivery, with Integration and Credential read and validated at the checkpoint.
- aggregate boundary: The rule's ordering clause is what fixes the boundary: 'claim one durable attempt before Integration/Credential validation'. The claim therefore commits on the Delivery root strictly before any Integration or Credential read, which is why a prepared-stage failure can be recorded against a real attempt rather than vanishing.
- value objects: DispatchCheckpoint, RequestDigest, ApplicationDeduplicationKeyDigest, ProviderCorrelationTokenDigest, ReplayMode, ReplayGeneration, DeliveryState, ReasonCode.
- domain service: Not applicable - enforced in the application commands and the adapter.
- repository: `DeliveryRepository`, `DeliveryAttemptRepository`, `DeliveryReconciliationRepository`, `NotificationEscalationRepository`, `NotificationReplayAcknowledgementRepository`; `IntegrationRepository` and `CredentialRepository` read-and-validate only.
- persistence model: Not applicable - PRULE-034 introduces no persistent record of its own; it constrains the records MTX-039 writes. Its one persistence-visible demand is that the attempt claim be durable before validation, which the `delivery_attempts` `prepared` checkpoint carries.
- migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added by this row. WITHHELD under OD-023: no rotation-token column, rotation DDL function or grant may be migrated.
- transaction boundary: The rule's own ordering: the durable attempt claim commits, THEN Integration and Credential validation runs inside that claimed attempt, THEN `submission_started` commits before any network write. The rule forbids collapsing these into one commit, because a claim that is not durable before validation cannot prove which attempt a prepared-stage failure belongs to.
- concurrency: One claimed attempt receives exactly one first submission and no attempt is resubmitted at or after `submission_started`. This is the rule's exact assertion in AC-PRULE-034 and is what makes at-least-once application processing safe without provider idempotency.
- idempotency: Application-level only, and the rule says so in both directions. It REQUIRES: at-least-once application attempt processing; one durable claim before validation; local deduplication such that duplicate consumption, redelivery, replay and concurrency reuse the attempt identity; and duplicate-tolerant retained action references so a duplicate email duplicates no authority or product action. It PROHIBITS: claiming provider exactly-once delivery, and treating permitted provider-visible duplicates as a defect. Mailgun supplies no provider-side idempotency and this contract asserts none.
- background job: Not applicable - the rule constrains the commands and workers, not a job of its own.
- queue: Not applicable - no queue of its own.
- retry policy: Not applicable - PRULE-034 defines no retry schedule of its own; it constrains which outcomes may retry. Its constraint is exact and exhaustive: retry only exhausted retryable initialization, proven no-network-submission, or definitive provider nonacceptance; disable implicit client and transport retry; suppress automatic resend while acceptance is unknown. The 1-, 5- and 30-minute schedule and the four-attempt bound belong to `notification-policy-v1` and are contracted in MTX-039.
- terminal failure: The rule requires nonretryable prepared-stage failures to terminalize rather than linger, and forbids a false terminal-failure claim. Absence of provider evidence is therefore never terminal: `acceptance_unknown` is the honest outcome and MUST NOT be converted to success or terminal failure.
- reconciliation: Read-only exact-token reconciliation is mandatory under the rule and never sends. The uncertain aggregate, the escalation and the user-visible status must all be exposed rather than hidden, which is the rule's transparency limb.
- domain events: Not applicable - PRULE-034 emits no event of its own; it constrains the seventeen WF-014 events and gates `NotificationReplayRequested` behind its acknowledgment requirement.
- event payload: Not applicable - no event of its own. The rule does bound every payload: no sensitive payload or credential leakage.
- event producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- event consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- serializer: Not applicable - no transport exposure.
- authorization entry point: Each command before mutation, and again before EVERY attempt - the rule's words are 'reauthorize/redact every attempt', so the per-attempt entry point is mandatory rather than a defensive extra.
- permission checks: The route's Required Permission per baseline route, re-evaluated at every attempt: `invitation.create`, `source.scope.propose`, `source.verify`, `history.read`, `score.summary.read`, `issue.read`, `issue.adjudicate`, `entitlement.notice.read`, `export.retrieve`, `security.notice.read`, plus the invitation binding for the direct Invitation route. `policy.notification.manage` for policy changes within each role's exact scope; `notification.replay` in an active support session for replay; `notification.inbox.read` for own-inbox reads. There is no customer connector catalogue, no arbitrary endpoint entry and no customer credential-entry journey, so no tenant can point delivery at a provider or credential of its own choosing.

A provider-visible duplicate after acknowledged replay or provider behavior is not an error when the local attempt claim and the underlying product action remain unique.
- audit record: As MTX-039. - retention: Not applicable - PRULE-034 defines no retention obligation of its own; the records it constrains fall in the `product_history` class owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md.
- test contracts: TYP-SEC: baseline Notifications route through in-app AND Mailgun email Deliveries - no third channel and no delayed channel exists. TYP-DATA: the direct intended-recipient Invitation exception applies exactly once and every other route uses Account permission selectors. TYP-SEC: only a valid platform-managed Integration and Credential is used; no customer connector catalogue, arbitrary endpoint entry or customer credential-entry journey exists. TYP-SEC: every attempt is reauthorized and redacted - authorization present at consumption and absent at attempt time yields `suppressed` and no provider call. TYP-DATA: email execution uses at-least-once APPLICATION attempt processing, asserted distinct from external delivery counts. TYP-DATA: one durable attempt is claimed BEFORE Integration and Credential validation - no Credential read occurs without a durable `prepared` row. TYP-DATA: nonretryable prepared-stage failures terminalize; they neither retry nor linger. TYP-DATA: retry admits exactly three classes and no fourth - exhausted retryable initialization, proven no-network-submission, and definitive provider nonacceptance. TYP-INT: implicit client and transport retry is disabled, asserted at the transport layer. TYP-DATA: `acceptance_unknown` applies whenever provider acceptance cannot be disproved, and automatic resend is suppressed while unknown. TYP-DATA: reconciliation is read-only and exact-token and never submits a message. TYP-OBS: the uncertain aggregate, the escalation and the user-visible status are all exposed. TYP-DATA: action references are duplicate-tolerant - the same logical action reference used twice produces one product transition. TYP-SEC: `delivery_replay` targets ONLY the same logical recipient and channel - a fixture asserting any other prior or current recipient, or the in-app channel, fails. TYP-SEC: NO EXACTLY-ONCE CLAIM is made anywhere - no code path, event, status, audit field, schema constraint or user-visible string asserts provider exactly-once delivery. TYP-INT: one prepared claim receives exactly one first submission and no attempt is resubmitted after `submission_started`, asserted under concurrency and under job redelivery. TYP-SEC: no false failure and no false success - absence of provider evidence yields neither. TYP-DATA: a permitted duplicate external email causes no duplicate authority and no duplicate product action. ### MTX-086 - AC-PRULE-035 (PRULE: PRULE-035)

- Slice: S-20
- Status: Complete

- interface type: A security rule constraining what an Export may contain, who may retrieve it and when it stops being retrievable. PRULE-035 governs CAP-022 and applies to WF-016 only. - route: Not applicable - PRULE-035 is a rule, not an interface. It constrains the retrieval and policy surfaces registered at MTX-041 and adds none of its own.
- request schema: Not applicable - PRULE-035 constrains the MTX-041 freeze and retrieval envelopes rather than defining one. It does add one requirement to the freeze input: the redaction result MUST be resolved server-side from the requester's current effective permissions and classification ceiling, so a client-asserted redaction scope is not an admissible input.
- response schema: Not applicable - see request_schema. The rule owns what the response may CONTAIN, which is exactly the frozen manifest scope and no more.
- controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter of its own; the rule constrains the MTX-041 controllers, none of which may widen a frozen scope or resolve a redaction.
- command: Enforced within `CreateExport`, `RetryExport`, `RequestExportApproval`, `DecideExportApproval`, `StartExportGeneration`, `CompleteExportGeneration`, `BeginExportRetrieval` and `ActivateExportPolicy`. This row adds no command.

- command output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-041 output. The rule's freeze clause fixes exactly what that output pins: one-Organization logical format, object, field and redaction scope; requester-as-recipient; versions; manifest; sizes; digests; and request hash.
- actor: Not applicable - the rule constrains content and reauthorization rather than a principal. The actors are fixed by WF-016; see MTX-041.
- organization scope: One Organization, frozen at creation. The rule's freeze clause names 'one-Organization logical format/object/field/redaction scope' as a single frozen unit, so scope cannot be widened after the freeze by any later policy, permission or command.
- aggregate: Export as the constrained root, with the immutable manifest as the artifact the rule protects and ExportPolicy as the versioned artifact it re-resolves.
- aggregate boundary: The rule fixes the boundary at the manifest: the manifest is written once and the lifecycle projection is written many times, and the two MUST NOT share a row. That is why `export_manifest_objects`, `export_manifest_fields` and `export_manifest_members` are `T-IMM` while `exports` is `T-MUT` - the rule's 'destroy package bytes without mutating the manifest' clause is enforced by table class rather than by discipline.
- value objects: RequestHash, ManifestHash, PackageSha256, MemberDigest, CompressedSize, UncompressedSize, FrozenManifestExpiresAt, EffectiveRetrievalExpiresAt, ExportPolicyVersion, RedactedFieldCode, ClassificationCeiling, ApprovalId, ApprovalExpiresAt.
- domain service: Not applicable - PRULE-035 names no domain service; it is enforced inside the application commands and at the retrieval checkpoints.
- repository: `ExportRepository` as the constrained write path over the Export and its manifest; `ExportPolicyRepository` read-only at freeze AND again at every retrieval, which is the rule's whole point - the policy is never cached from the freeze.
- persistence model: Not applicable as a new concept - PRULE-035 introduces no persistent record; it constrains the rows MTX-041 writes. The rule is nevertheless enforced BY persistence: the three manifest tables are `T-IMM` so no lifecycle timestamp can reach them; `exports` carries the frozen scope, hash and redaction codes alongside the mutable state and times, keeping the two separable; `export_approvals` carries a single-use unique used attempt so one approval cannot authorize two generations; and `export_retrievals` stores no reusable URL so no retrieval can outlive its authorization.
- migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added; the constraints the rule relies on are already declared in schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md. WITHHELD under OD-031: as MTX-041, no retention-cursor artifact for the `product_history`-class Export record or manifest may be migrated.
- transaction boundary: The rule states its own: the freeze is atomic, the manifest commits once and is never reopened, and retrieval reauthorizes against CURRENT permission and policy inside its own short transaction rather than reusing the freeze's decision. Package byte destruction occurs without any transaction touching the manifest.
- concurrency: Expiry-wins is the rule's mechanism and it is stated as an equality rule rather than a race: at `now_utc >= effective_retrieval_expires_at` the expiry checkpoint wins over retrieval, and at the exact approval expiry instant expiry wins over generation start. Neither is decided by arrival order. The single-use approval is consumed atomically at generation start, so concurrent generation attempts cannot both proceed. A policy contraction and an in-flight retrieval do not race for correctness: retrieval resolves the then-active policy at checkpoint 3, so a contraction committed before it denies and one committed after it cannot retract bytes already emitted.
- idempotency: The rule names one obligation this row keeps exact: ONE new approval per high-risk create or retry GENERATION ATTEMPT. The approval is therefore not idempotent across attempts by design - reusing it is the defect the single-use unique used attempt exists to prevent - while the create or retry COMMAND remains idempotent by its own identity, so an exact replay returns the original result and consumes no second approval. Those two rules coexist because replay and retry are different things: a replay reuses the attempt, a retry is a new attempt and needs a new approval.
- background job: Not applicable as a job of its own - the rule constrains commands and checkpoints. Its package-destruction clause names an obligation whose execution has NO registered dispatch surface in Volume II; that gap is recorded at MTX-041 and no job, work type or ScheduledAction kind is invented here to fill it.
- queue: Not applicable - PRULE-035 introduces no queue.
- retry policy: Not applicable - PRULE-035 defines no retry and forbids the shape of one that would bypass its approval rule: a new generation attempt is a new approval, so an automatic retry of a failed high-risk generation would silently reuse authorization the rule requires to be re-obtained.
- terminal failure: The rule's three zero-byte retrieval terminals, each exact: current permission or policy narrower than the frozen manifest denies the WHOLE package with `export_scope_no_longer_authorized` and never partially strips it; a missing or invalid current policy denies with `policy_unavailable`, so retrieval fails CLOSED; and at or after the effective retrieval expiry the checkpoint returns `export_expired`. A size, digest, scope or manifest violation fails generation and publishes no retrieval option.
- reconciliation: The rule reconciles access against CURRENT state at every retrieval rather than against a projection: `min(frozen_manifest_expires_at, available_at_utc + current_policy_lifetime)` is recomputed per retrieval, and current format, field, compressed-size and uncompressed-size bounds are re-applied to the frozen manifest each time. A shortened policy therefore takes effect at the next retrieval regardless of whether its reevaluation job has run. WITHHELD under OD-031: no retention-cursor reconciler for the `product_history` Export record and manifest exists.
- domain events: Not applicable - PRULE-035 emits no event of its own; it gates `ExportRequested`, `ExportAvailable`, `ExportFailed`, `ExportExpired`, `ExportRevoked`, `ExportRetrieved` and `ExportPolicyActivated`.
- event payload: Not applicable - no event of its own. The rule does constrain every payload: `redacted_field_codes` describe omitted fields only and never reveal their values.
- event producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- event consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- serializer: Not applicable - PRULE-035 constrains logical content and expressly not bytes; it freezes a LOGICAL format and allowlist, and acceptance validates decoded objects and declared digests rather than a byte sequence.
- authorization entry point: The retrieval checkpoint, reauthorizing against CURRENT permission and policy, and the freeze checkpoint, resolving redaction from current authority. The rule's SEC-REQ-014 linkage is why the retrieval recheck is a security property rather than a freshness nicety: an Export is a durable copy of authorized data, so an authorization decision that is not re-evaluated at the moment bytes are emitted is a bypass regardless of how correct it was at freeze.
- permission checks: The rule adds no permission and grants none. It constrains how the MTX-041 tokens are applied: `export.retrieve` is re-evaluated at every retrieval and its CURRENT field scope is compared against the frozen manifest, so losing a field permission after the freeze denies the whole package. `evidence.restricted.read` is the independent gate deciding whether restricted Evidence fields could enter the frozen scope at all. `security.investigation.approve` must be held by a DIFFERENT active SecurityOperator for each high-risk generation attempt. `policy.export.manage` may only narrow.
- tenant boundary: The one-Organization scope is frozen at creation and is part of the same atomic freeze as format, fields and redaction, so it cannot be widened later. Multi-Organization export is prohibited and a combined package is always rejected; WF-018 submits one separate approved Export per Organization. Requester-as-recipient is frozen too, so an Export cannot be redirected to another principal after authorization.
- error contract: As MTX-041's retrieval terminals - `export_scope_no_longer_authorized` denying the whole package, `policy_unavailable` failing closed, and `export_expired` with expiry owning equality - plus rejection of a reused, altered or self-approved approval BEFORE reservation or generation. A generation-time manifest mismatch, omitted selected object, extra object or field, digest mismatch, size excess or unsupported logical format fails generation and publishes no retrieval option.
- audit record: The frozen scope and its `redacted_field_codes`, the policy and artifact versions the freeze pinned and the policy version each retrieval resolved, every manifest field, digest and size, the approval identity and its approver, the retrieval authorization decision and time, and the correlation ID. The two policy versions - frozen and current-at-retrieval - are both recorded precisely because the rule's entire subject is the gap between them.
- observability: A retrieval denied by `export_scope_no_longer_authorized` or `policy_unavailable` is distinguishable in telemetry from one denied by `export_expired`, because the first two indicate an authorization or policy change since the freeze and the third is the ordinary lifecycle end. A package whose bytes are past their `delivery_package` maximum while the record remains `product_history` is observable as the recorded destruction gap rather than being silently assumed destroyed.
- retention: Both classes, and the split IS the rule: `delivery_package` covers the encrypted package bytes ONLY, with a maximum at the earlier of manifest expiry, revocation, or 24 hours after availability and destruction by cryptographic key destruction plus primary and cache deletion, while the Export record and manifest remain `product_history` at 7 years. That is what 'destroy package bytes without mutating the manifest' means concretely, and it is why the destruction of one class leaves the other intact and auditable. `delivery_package` is excluded from backup coverage. `retention-interim-v1` is the FIXED approved baseline under resolved OD-011 despite its name and is not customer-configurable. WITHHELD under OD-031: the routine retention-expiry destruction trigger for the `product_history`-class Export record and manifest at their 7-year maximum where no accepted deletion or closure request exists. The `delivery_package` limb is not withheld by OD-031, but its execution has no registered dispatch surface; see the recorded gap at MTX-041.
- test contracts: TYP-SEC: the freeze is atomic and complete - format, one-Organization object and field scope, redaction result, artifact versions, requester-as-recipient, policy, approval when required and request hash all commit together or not at all; no partially frozen Export reaches generation. TYP-SEC: the frozen allowlist names every included object ID and logical field and no unlisted object or field appears in the decoded package. TYP-SEC: redaction is resolved server-side from the requester's current effective permissions and ceiling; a client-supplied redaction scope cannot widen it. TYP-SEC: Evidence payload bytes and restricted fields are excluded unless the requester independently holds the read permission AND the active policy allows them. TYP-DATA: `redacted_field_codes` uses the stable groups and appends the exact snake-case logical field name when only some fields in a group are omitted; codes describe omitted fields only and never reveal values. TYP-SEC: requester-as-recipient is frozen - an Export cannot be redirected to another principal after authorization. TYP-SEC: multi-Organization export is rejected and a combined package is always rejected; WF-018 submits one separate approved Export per Organization. TYP-DATA: the size bounds are exact at 104857600 encrypted and 262144000 total uncompressed, asserted at the bound and one either side. TYP-DATA: an Organization policy may remove formats, lower either size, shorten lifetime or remove fields and can NEVER broaden the baseline. TYP-SEC: ONE new approval per high-risk create or retry GENERATION ATTEMPT - a reused, altered or self-approved approval, or a retry with none, is rejected before reservation and generation, asserted by observing that no entitlement reservation exists on the rejected path. TYP-DATA: the approval expires exactly one hour after `approved_at_utc`, and creation and the immediate `Pending -> Generating` checkpoint must BOTH commit before it; at the exact expiry instant expiry WINS. TYP-DATA: a create or retry COMMAND replay returns the original result and consumes no second approval, proving replay and retry are distinguished. TYP-SEC: retrieval reauthorizes against CURRENT permission and policy and never reuses the freeze decision - a field permission lost after the freeze denies the WHOLE package with `export_scope_no_longer_authorized`, asserted to be never partially stripped. TYP-SEC: a missing or invalid current policy denies with `policy_unavailable` and zero bytes, proving retrieval fails CLOSED. TYP-DATA: the effective retrieval expiry is exactly `min(frozen_manifest_expires_at, available_at_utc + current_policy_lifetime)`, and expiry OWNS equality, asserted immediately before, exactly at and immediately after the instant. TYP-DATA: current format, field, compressed-size and uncompressed-size bounds are re-applied to the frozen manifest at every retrieval. TYP-DATA: a policy shortened after availability denies at the next retrieval regardless of whether its reevaluation job has run. TYP-DATA: a policy lengthened after availability cannot move the effective expiry later than the frozen manifest expiry. TYP-DATA: `delivery_package` is asserted excluded from backup coverage, so no backup path resurrects destroyed bytes. TYP-DATA: `retention-interim-v1` is asserted to be the FIXED approved baseline under resolved OD-011 - no customer-configurable retention path exists and configurability is asserted never inferred from the fixed policy. ### MTX-087 - AC-PRULE-036 (PRULE: PRULE-036)

- Slice: S-20
- Status: Complete
- contract owner: specification/volume-ii/APPLICATION_LAYER.md#prule-036-export-lifecycle-transitions
- interface type: A lifecycle rule fixing the complete Export state machine and the immutability of the package manifest across it. PRULE-036 governs CAP-022 and applies to WF-016 only. Its decision dependency OD-011 is RESOLVED with `Blocking Impact: None for Volume I`, so nothing in the transition set is withheld. It is a rule, not an interface.
- route: Not applicable - PRULE-036 is a rule, not an interface. It constrains the transitions reachable from the routes registered at MTX-041 and adds none of its own.
- request schema: Not applicable - PRULE-036 constrains transitions rather than defining an envelope. It does add one requirement to every human command input: the expected state version, without which a stale transition cannot be detected and rejected.
- response schema: Not applicable - see request_schema. The rule owns which states a response may report, not its shape.
- controller: Not applicable - no HTTP adapter of its own; the rule constrains what the MTX-041 controllers may reach.
- command: Enforced within `CreateExport`, `StartExportGeneration`, `CompleteExportGeneration`, `FailExportGeneration`, `RetryExport`, `RevokeExport` and `ExpireExport`. This row adds no command.
- command input: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-041 input; see request_schema for the expected-state-version requirement it adds.
- command output: Not applicable - constrains the MTX-041 output to exactly one of the six declared states.
- actor: Not applicable - the rule constrains transitions rather than a principal, and it applies identically to every actor. The one actor distinction it preserves is structural rather than its own: `Available -> Expired` is reachable only by the export lifecycle service under `export.expire` and by no human, so a rule about states also fixes who can reach one.
- organization scope: The Export's one frozen Organization; every transition resolves within it and none can move an Export between Organizations.
- aggregate: Export as the constrained root; the immutable manifest as the artifact the rule protects from lifecycle writes; the retry-linked successor Export as a separate root carrying `retry_of_export_id`.
- aggregate boundary: The rule's manifest clause fixes the boundary and it is the same one PRULE-035 relies on from the security side: lifecycle state and times live on the mutable `exports` root, and the manifest lives in three `T-IMM` child tables. A retry does not reopen the failed Export's boundary at all - it creates a NEW linked Export with its own manifest, which is why `Failed -> Pending` is a transition of the successor rather than a resurrection of the predecessor.
- value objects: ExportState (`pending`, `generating`, `available`, `failed`, `expired`, `revoked`), ExportStateVersion, RetryOfExportId, ManifestHash, PackageSha256, RevokedAt, ExpiredAt, TerminalReasonCode, CorrelationId.
- domain service: Not applicable - PRULE-036 names no domain service; the transition guard is a pure total function over the current state, the expected version and the requested edge, applied inside the application commands.
- repository: `ExportRepository` as the constrained write path; the manifest repositories are append-only at generation completion and expose no update path at all, which is what makes the rule's immutability clause structural.
- persistence model: Not applicable as a new concept - PRULE-036 introduces no persistent record; it constrains the `exports` row MTX-041 writes. The rule is nevertheless enforced BY persistence: `exports.state CHECK ('pending','generating','available','failed','expired','revoked')` bounds the state set to exactly the six the rule admits, and the separation of `requested/generating/available/expiry/revoked/failed` times on the mutable root from the `T-IMM` manifest tables is what makes 'lifecycle timestamps never mutate its immutable package manifest' true by construction rather than by convention.
- migration: Not applicable - no schema object is added; the `state CHECK` and the manifest tables' `T-IMM` class are already declared in schemas/POSTGRESQL_SCHEMA.md. No migration, function or grant may admit an edge outside the declared set.
- transaction boundary: Each transition is its own commit against the Export root under its expected state version. The manifest commit at `Generating -> Available` is the only write the manifest tables ever receive; no later transition opens a transaction that touches them.
- concurrency: Fixed winners rather than arrival order. At `now_utc >= effective_retrieval_expires_at` the expiry checkpoint wins over retrieval. A revocation and a timed expiry racing on one available Export resolve to exactly one terminal, because both are guarded by the expected state version and `expired` and `revoked` are absorbing - the loser observes a stale version and changes nothing. Two concurrent retries of one failed Export cannot both create a successor: each carries the expected state version of the predecessor and only one commits. A stale or replayed transition never wins by being late; it is rejected and audited.
- idempotency: The rule's replay clause is exact and this row keeps its three cases separate. An EXACT REPLAY of a transition command returns the original result and emits no second event and no second transition. A STALE transition - one carrying an expected state version that no longer matches - is rejected and audited as invalid, changing nothing. An INVALID transition - one naming an edge outside the declared set - is likewise rejected and audited, changing nothing, and no schema, migration, function or grant admits it. The distinction matters because all three arrive as the same shape of request and only the first is benign.
- background job: Not applicable as a job of its own - the rule constrains commands. Two of the transitions it governs are reached from jobs: `Generating -> Available` and `Generating -> Failed` from `export_generate`, and `Available -> Expired` from `export_expire`. The rule constrains those edges identically to human-reached ones; a job enjoys no relaxed transition guard.
- queue: Not applicable - PRULE-036 introduces no queue.
- retry policy: Not applicable as an automatic retry - the rule DEFINES what a retry is and it is not an automatic one: `Failed -> Pending` occurs only through an authorized LINKED retry command. An automatic retry would reach the same edge without the authorization, entitlement reservation and, for high-risk content, the new approval the linked command carries, which is precisely why the rule words the edge as it does.
- terminal failure: `available` is not terminal. `failed` is terminal but recoverable only through the authorized linked retry that creates a successor. `expired` and `revoked` are absorbing and no path reopens them. Every invalid, stale or replayed transition attempt is rejected and audited under SM-REQ-007 and changes no state.
- reconciliation: The rule's own consistency check is the transition audit: OBS-REQ-006 requires every transition attempt - accepted, invalid, stale or replayed - to be auditable, so a rejected attempt leaves evidence rather than vanishing. That is what makes 'every invalid/stale/replayed transition is rejected/audited' verifiable after the fact rather than only at the moment of rejection.
- domain events: Not applicable - PRULE-036 emits no event of its own; it gates the seven lifecycle events `ExportRequested`, `ExportGenerating`, `ExportAvailable`, `ExportFailed`, `ExportExpired`, `ExportRevoked` and, through the retry edge, the successor's `ExportRequested`. A rejected transition emits no lifecycle event and exactly one denial audit event.
- event payload: Not applicable - no event of its own. The rule constrains the payloads it gates to carry the from-state, to-state, expected state version and terminal reason code, so a transition event is reconstructible without recomputation.
- event producer: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- event consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.
- serializer: Not applicable - PRULE-036 has no transport representation of its own; its subject is the state machine behind the MTX-041 surfaces.
- authorization entry point: The command handler, before mutation, and the lifecycle-service expiry checkpoint for the one edge no human may reach. The rule's SM-REQ-007 linkage makes the transition guard itself a correctness boundary: an edge outside the declared set is a defect regardless of whether the actor was authorized for the command that requested it.
- permission checks: The rule adds no permission and grants none, but it is where the state machine and the permission table meet: `Failed -> Pending` requires `export.retry`, `Available -> Revoked` requires `export.revoke`, and `Available -> Expired` requires the lifecycle service's `export.expire`, which the Permission Baseline denies to EVERY role. So the one transition no human can request is the one the rule most needs to be automatic and exactly-once.
- tenant boundary: Every transition resolves within the Export's one frozen Organization under proved RLS context; no edge moves an Export between Organizations and no cross-Organization command reaches a transition guard.
- error contract: An invalid edge, a stale expected state version and a replayed transition are three distinct outcomes: the first two return `F1-DOMAIN-409` and are audited as invalid transitions under SM-REQ-007 with no state change, while an exact replay returns the ORIGINAL result rather than an error and emits nothing further. Authorization denial on a transition command returns `F1-AUTH-403`, emits one authorization audit event and performs no state change.
- audit record: Every transition attempt - accepted, invalid, stale or replayed - with the from-state, to-state, expected and actual state versions, the actor or lifecycle service identity, the terminal reason code, the retry lineage linking a successor to its predecessor, and the correlation ID. Per OBS-REQ-006 a rejected attempt is audited as fully as an accepted one, which is what makes an attempted invalid transition detectable rather than merely ineffective.
- observability: The lifecycle projection times - requested, generating, available, expiry, revoked, failed - make each transition observable in order, and DLC-REQ-014 is satisfied by their living on the mutable root while the manifest stays immutable. An invalid or stale transition attempt is observable as an audited rejection, so a client repeatedly attempting a forbidden edge is visible rather than silent. A retry is observable as a linked successor rather than as a reopened predecessor.
- retention: The Export lifecycle record and its manifest are `product_history` at 7 years; the package bytes alone are `delivery_package` and their destruction leaves both intact, which is exactly the rule's manifest-immutability guarantee expressed as a retention split. Windows are owned by 015 DATA_LIFECYCLE.md and this row states none. WITHHELD under OD-031: the routine retention-expiry destruction trigger for the `product_history`-class Export record and manifest at their 7-year maximum where no accepted Account deletion or Organization closure request exists.
- test contracts: TYP-INT: the complete declared transition set and nothing else - `Pending -> Generating`, `Generating -> Available`, `Generating -> Failed`, `Available -> Expired`, `Available -> Revoked`, and `Failed -> Pending` ONLY through an authorized linked retry. TYP-INT: each undeclared edge asserted ABSENT and rejected - `Available -> Failed`, `Available -> Generating`, `Expired -> Available`, `Expired -> Revoked`, `Revoked -> Available`, `Revoked -> Expired`, `Pending -> Available`, `Pending -> Failed`, `Failed -> Available`, `Failed -> Generating` and `Generating -> Pending` each change no state and are logged as invalid transitions under SM-REQ-007. TYP-DATA: `exports.state CHECK` admits exactly `pending`, `generating`, `available`, `failed`, `expired`, `revoked` and no schema, migration, function or grant admits another value or edge. TYP-DATA: `expired` and `revoked` are ABSORBING - no path reopens them, asserted for every command including an authorized retry. TYP-DATA: `Failed -> Pending` requires `export.retry`, a NEW entitlement reservation and, for high-risk content, a NEW single-use approval; a retry missing any one of the three changes nothing. TYP-DATA: a retry creates a NEW linked Export carrying `retry_of_export_id` and does NOT mutate the failed predecessor, whose state, manifest and reason are asserted unchanged. TYP-SEC: `Available -> Expired` is reachable ONLY by the export lifecycle service under `export.expire`; a human command asserting expiry is denied and changes nothing, and `export.expire` is asserted deny for every role including OrganizationAdmin and SecurityOperator. TYP-SEC: `Available -> Revoked` requires `export.revoke`, and a MarketingOperator or TechnicalImplementer may reach it only for an Export they requested. TYP-DATA: a stale expected state version on any transition command is rejected with `F1-DOMAIN-409`, audited as an invalid transition, and changes nothing. TYP-DATA: the three manifest tables expose no update path - an attempted manifest update is rejected by table class, not by application check. TYP-INT: a revocation and a timed expiry racing on one available Export resolve to exactly one terminal and the loser changes nothing. TYP-DATA: the lifecycle projection times are written in order and each transition is reconstructible from its own persisted fields without recomputation. - event consumers: Not applicable - no event of its own.

A remediation attempted directly from the report is refused with no side effect. `export_scope_no_longer_authorized` when a current-policy contraction makes the package ineligible; the package is never partially stripped. `policy_unavailable` on a missing or invalid current Export Policy.

Every permitted high-risk attempt records its `approval_id`, Organization, requester, approver, logical format, exact object and field allowlists, request hash, `approved_at_utc`, `expires_at_utc`, `used_by_export_id` and state version. WF-018's Audit and Observability requires the Export IDs and the linked remediation to be persisted on the Investigation, so the report's inertness is provable from the Investigation's own record.

The Export package's own manifest, retrieval expiry and lifecycle are WF-016's and are owned by S-20.

TYP-SEC: the approval NEVER substitutes for the underlying workflow permission - the fixture asserts `export.create` is checked independently and that `security.investigate` grants neither `export.create` nor the approval. TYP-SEC: an unscoped export is denied and audited.
